morningLine: This week at the counter: TI software policy arguments, Apple II arcade conversions, IBM PC XT talk, and Michael Jackson still holding the radio.

lead.headline: TI software control sparks game-counter argument
lead.dek: Arcade Express reported Texas Instruments wanted tighter control over TI-99/4A software, a sign that cartridge economics and home-computer publishing were colliding.
lead.body: The April 10 Arcade Express reached readers at the start of this Chronicle week with a sharp business-of-games lead: Texas Instruments wanted to keep control of software for the TI-99/4A. For dealers, publishers, and families watching the low-cost computer aisle, the question was not academic. A machine could be attractive on price and still be defined by who was allowed to publish for it, how cartridges reached shelves, and whether independent game makers could fill the rack quickly enough.

market.headline: Software shelves decide the home-computer fight
